**Overview**

This dashboard provides a centralized view of security findings from AWS GuardDuty. It visualizes data based on severity levels, regions, and resource types, allowing teams to assess potential threats in their cloud environments. Summary metrics help highlight the overall volume and severity of findings, while time-series and categorical breakdowns assist in identifying trends and common threat sources. Filters can be used to refine the results by cloud provider, region, or account for more focused investigations.

[{"embeddableConfig":{"description":"","enhancements":{"dynamicActions":{"events":[]}},"savedVis":{"data":{"aggs":[],"searchSource":{"filter":[],"query":{"language":"kuery","query":""}}},"description":"","id":"","params":{"fontSize":12,"markdown":"##### Elastic Load Balancer (ELB)
Elastic Load Balancing automatically distributes your incoming traffic across multiple targets, such as EC2 instances, containers, and IP addresses, in one or more Availability Zones. It monitors the health of its registered targets, and routes traffic only to the healthy targets. 

##### Application Load Balancer (ALB)
An Application Load Balancer is a tool that helps manage and distribute web traffic to different servers or services. By analyzing incoming traffic, it can route requests based on specific rules, such as URL paths or HTTP methods, allowing for more efficient handling of complex applications. 

##### Network Load Balancer (NLB)
Network Load Balancer operates at the connection level (Layer 4), routing connections to targets (Amazon EC2 instances, microservices, and containers) within Amazon VPC, based on IP protocol data. Ideal for load balancing of both TCP and UDP traffic, handling millions of requests per second while maintaining ultra-low latencies.","openLinksInNewTab":false},"title":"","type":"markdown","uiState":{}}},"gridData":{"h":19,"i":"a9e983e6-f1cc-4927-bddf-1cdceabb2d9c","w":26,"x":0,"y":0},"panelIndex":"a9e983e6-f1cc-4927-bddf-1cdceabb2d9c","title":"","type":"visualization"},{"embeddableConfig":{"description":"","enhancements":{"dynamicActions":{"events":[]}},"savedVis":{"data":{"aggs":[],"searchSource":{"filter":[],"query":{"language":"kuery","query":""}}},"description":"","id":"","params":{"fontSize":12,"markdown":"[ELB Overview](#/view/aws-eab04366-1114-4ab0-ac49-9041e0a584b1)

This dashboard provides an overview of AWS Config rule evaluations, enabling security and compliance teams to monitor resource configurations across their AWS environment. attributes.title: [Elastic Agent] Entity Analytics Input Metrics

esqlQuery.esql:
FROM metrics-system*
| WHERE TO_LOWER(process.executable) LIKE "*elastic*agent*" AND agent.name NOT LIKE "*agentless*"
| STATS cpu_process_pct = MAX(system.process.cpu.total.norm.pct) * 100
    BY elastic_agent.id, process.name,
      time_bucket = BUCKET(@timestamp, 1 minute)
// Count the 1 minute timebuckets that are above 80% by process and agent
| WHERE cpu_process_pct >= 80
| STATS count_above_threshold = COUNT(*)
    BY elastic_agent.id, process.name
// Alert if there are 5 or more occurences
| WHERE count_above_threshold >= 5

FROM metrics-elastic_agent.*beat-*
| WHERE data_stream.dataset LIKE "elastic_agent.*beat" AND agent.name NOT LIKE "*agentless*"
| STATS 
  events_dropped_max = max(to_long(beat.stats.libbeat.pipeline.events.dropped)),
  events_dropped_min = min(to_long(beat.stats.libbeat.pipeline.events.dropped)), 
  pipeline_acked_max = max(to_long(beat.stats.libbeat.pipeline.queue.acked)), 
  pipeline_acked_min = min(to_long(beat.stats.libbeat.pipeline.queue.acked)) 
  BY time_bucket = DATE_TRUNC(1 minute, @timestamp), elastic_agent.id, component.id
| EVAL 
  events_dropped = events_dropped_max - events_dropped_min, 
  events_acked = pipeline_acked_max - pipeline_acked_min
| EVAL drop_pct = CASE(
  events_acked > 0, events_dropped / events_acked, 
  0
)
| WHERE drop_pct >= 0.05
| STATS MAX(drop_pct) BY elastic_agent.id, component.id

FROM metrics-system*
| WHERE TO_LOWER(process.executable) LIKE "*elastic*agent*" AND agent.name NOT LIKE "*agentless*"
| STATS max_memory_per_process = MAX(system.process.memory.rss.pct * 100) BY agent.id, process.name
| STATS total_memory_usage = SUM(max_memory_per_process) BY agent.id
| WHERE total_memory_usage > 50

FROM logs-elastic_agent-*
| WHERE message like "Starting*elastic-agent*"
| STATS restart_count = count(*) BY host.name, bucket(@timestamp,5 minute)
| WHERE restart_count > 10
| STATS MAX(restart_count) BY host.name

FROM metrics-elastic_agent.*beat-*
| WHERE data_stream.dataset LIKE "elastic_agent.*beat" AND agent.name NOT LIKE "*agentless*"
| STATS pipeline_queue_pct = MAX(beat.stats.libbeat.pipeline.queue.filled.pct) * 100 BY elastic_agent.id, component.id
| WHERE pipeline_queue_pct >= 90

FROM logs-elastic_agent.status_change-default
| WHERE data_stream.dataset == "elastic_agent.status_change" and agentless == false and health_status == "offline"

FROM metrics-elastic_agent.*beat-*
| WHERE data_stream.dataset LIKE "elastic_agent.*beat" AND agent.name NOT LIKE "*agentless*"
| STATS 
    max_errors = MAX(TO_LONG(beat.stats.libbeat.output.write.errors)),
    min_errors = MIN(TO_LONG(beat.stats.libbeat.output.write.errors))  
    BY time_bucket = DATE_TRUNC(1 minute, @timestamp), elastic_agent.id, component.id
| EVAL errors_count = max_errors - min_errors 
| WHERE errors_count > 5 
| STATS MAX(errors_count) BY elastic_agent.id, component.id

FROM logs-elastic_agent.status_change-default
| WHERE data_stream.dataset == "elastic_agent.status_change" and agentless == false and health_status == "unenrolled"

FROM logs-elastic_agent.status_change-default
| WHERE data_stream.dataset == "elastic_agent.status_change" and agentless == false and health_status == "unhealthy"

FROM logs-elastic_agent.status_change-default
| WHERE data_stream.dataset == "elastic_agent.status_change" and agentless == false and health_status == "uninstalled"

Overview — multi-cloud + LLM spend
Cost allocation — account, subscription, service, team, tag, region
Engineering & Ops — usage correlated with cost
Historical cost & 7-day run-rate forecast
LLM traces — end-to-end call, tokens, and cost
Token usage per request — prompt, completion, total
LLM cost — model, user, feature, team
LLM quality & latency
Funnel — which user flows consume the most tokens

attributes.title: [Meridian] FinOps & LLM Observability

attributes.description: Cross-cloud cost allocation (account, subscription, service, team, tag, region), usage-to-cost correlation, historical spend and 7-day run-rate forecast, native provider FinOps links, and LLM observability: traces, tokens, cost, quality, latency, and user-flow funnel. Snapshot of the working dashboard from 2026-08-17.
